quotes.text: A database stores facts. Dataverse stores facts plus meaning, relationships, ownership, security boundaries, metadata, and life cycle behavior that travel with the data across apps, automation, and increasingly AI.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Crisp definition of why Dataverse is a semantics engine rather than plain storage.

quotes.text: If you want a simple leadership test for Dataverse, ask who owns the model. Not who built the app, who owns the model.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A one-line test leaders can apply immediately to expose missing data ownership.

quotes.text: Tables are nouns, processes are verbs. A table should represent a business noun that exists across time.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable modeling rule that prevents screen-driven schemas.

quotes.text: This is why prompt engineering is not a strategy. It's a tax you pay for ambiguity. If your data model is precise, prompts can be simple.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Connects AI answer quality directly to data model quality.

quotes.text: Smart teams measure success by how boring the model becomes. If the model stops changing every week, that's not stagnation. That's stability.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes a stable schema as the real success metric of a platform.

takeaways: Dataverse is a business semantics engine, so tables, columns and relationships are commitments about what the business believes is true, not UI scaffolding.
Data modeling is leadership work: name and own the core business concepts, design relationship behavior deliberately, and protect the model with environments and managed solutions.
AI and agents consume whatever meaning the model makes explicit, so ownership, security roles, descriptions and relationships become the foundation for reliable grounding and agent memory.
hook: Most Power Platform failures start at the data layer, when Dataverse is treated like a nicer place to store rows and the first app shapes the model. This episode, inspired by Bülent Altinsoy's Dataverse workshop, is for makers, architects and leaders who want to understand why smart data models, relationships, security and ALM decide whether apps, audits and AI agents scale or drift.
